courses.title: Introduction to Administration of Justice
courses.instructor: Stephen P. Choi, Simon Z. Sarkis, Jeffrey R. Hislop, Thomas E. Trindad, Chou Her, Frank J. Drummond
courses.description: ADJU 201-INTRODUCTION TO ADMINISTRATION OF JUSTICE 3 UNITS 54 Lecture Hours, 108 Out-of-Class Hours Total Student Learning Hours= 162 Exploration of the history and philosophy of the administration of justice system in America including the intricate workings of the police, the courts and corrections systems. Focus is placed on examining crime measurement, theoretical explanations of crime, responses to crime, punishment, components of the system and the current challenges to the system. Students are introduced to the origins and development of criminal law, legal process and sentencing, incarceration policies and ethics in the administration of justice field. Field trips might be required. (A-F Only) Transfer: (CSU, UC) General Education: Using catalog rights, check catalog for course general education approvals. courses.title: Healthcare Systems
courses.description: HE 107- HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS 3 UNITS 54.00 Lecture Hours, 108.00 Out-of-Class Hours, 162.00 Total Student Learning Hours This course provides students with an understanding of the U.S. healthcare system and health insurance options to provide for efficient navigation through the healthcare system. Topics include the history of health insurance in the U.S. and the role of government in healthcare; the U.S. healthcare workforce; basic health insurance terminology; types of insurance and the healthcare marketplace; different types of care, including outpatient, ambulatory and long-term care; public assistance programs and disability programs; and ethical and bioethical issues. Not Repeatable. Field trips not required. Transfers to CSU and UC. (A-F or P/NP) (C-ID: PH 110) General Education: Using catalog rights, check catalog for course general education approvals. For further clarification, see a counselor.

courses.title: Movies With a Message
courses.description: SJS 154-MOVIES WITH A MESSAGE 3 UNITS 54 Lecture Hours, 108 Out-of-Class Hours, Total Student Learning Hours=162 Aimed at using the medium of film to broaden the awareness of current societal and global issues, focusing on different topics semester to semester. Selected sequences of feature films, documentaries, unusual foreign and domestic releases will explore how film makers depict aspects of history, culture, religion, race, gender, class, ideology and other issues in a global perspective. Course will cover related elements of film style and theory, such as the relationship of subject to style, form and function. Modern variations on film media (animation, YouTube, reality TV and device media) will be investigated with an eye on 21st century culture. Formerly SOCSC 154. Field trips might be required. Not repeatable. (A-F or P/NP) Transfer: (CSU, UC) General Education: Using catalog rights, check catalog for course general education approvals. For further clarification, see a counselor.

courses.description: KIN 102- PSYCHOLOGICAL ASPECTS OF SPORT PERFORMANCE, 3 UNITS (Formerly titled as: Exercise and sport Psychology) Formerly listed as: PE 109: Peak Performance Through Mental Training 54 Lecture Hours, 108 Out-of-Class Hours, Total Student Learning Hours=162 Investigation of current theoretical perspectives, research, and applications of theory and techniques related to the field of sport psychology. courses.description: HE 111-WOMEN'S HEALTH, 3 UNITS 54 Lecture Hours, 108 Out-of-Class Hours, Total Student Learning Hours=162 Introduces students to psychological, sociocultural and biological aspects of women's health and explores health services, health education, and healthcare delivery systems. Social determinants of health and health inequities are examined as well as contemporary issues. The course draws on theoretical frameworks from sociology, psychology, and feminist studies to explore the impact of institutions, policies, and cultural norms on women's physical, mental, and social health across the lifespan. courses.description: KIN 100-INTRODUCTION TO KINESIOLOGY 3 UNITS Formerly listed as: PE 124: Introduction to Kinesiology 54 Lecture Hours, 108 Out-of-Class Hours, Total Student Learning Hours=162 Fundamental concepts concerning the interaction of biological and mechanical aspects of the musculoskeletal and neuromuscular structures. This course combines anatomy and kinesiology by addressing the anatomical structure and function of the musculoskeletal system as it relates to human movement and exercise. Muscular analysis and practical application, including strengthening and flexibility exercises for each muscle, will be emphasized. Students will also study physiological and biomechanical principles. Emphasis on the importance of the sub-disciplines such as; motor learning, motor development, biomechanics, exercise physiology, nutrition, and sports psychology in Kinesiology will be discussed along with career opportunities in the areas of teaching, coaching, allied health, and fitness professions. Field trips are not required. Not repeatable. courses.description: GEOG 102-CULTURAL GEOGRAPHY 3 Units 54 Lecture Hours, 108 Out-of-Class Hours, Total Student Learning Hours=162 Introduction to origins and global distribution of cultures. courses.title: Global Health
courses.description: HE 109 - GLOBAL HEALTH 3 UNITS 54 LECTURE HOURS, 108 OUT-OF-CLASS HOURS, 162 TOTAL STUDENT LEARNING HOURS Introduces the growing field of global health, global health challenges, programs, and policies through theoretical foundations and research methods. courses.description: HE 115-DRUGS, HEALTH, AND SOCIETY 3 UNITS 54 Lecture Hours, 108 Out-of-Class Hours, Total Student Learning Hours=162 Explores substance use and abuse, focusing on how individual behavior, social environments, and public health interact. courses.description: HE 112-INTRODUCTION TO PUBLIC HEALTH 3 UNITS 54 Lecture Hours, 108 Out-of-Class Hours, Total Student Learning Hours=162 Introduces public health, emphasizing how social, cultural, economic, and environmental factors influence health behaviors and outcomes. Topics include population health challenges, social determinants of health, epidemiology of infectious and chronic diseases, prevention and control strategies, community health promotion, environmental health, global health, and healthcare policy. Students will explore strategies to reduce health disparities and promote health equity across populations. Field trips are not required. Not repeatable. courses.title: Social Determinants of Health, Disparities and Equities
courses.description: HE 113 - SOCIAL DETERMINATION OF HEALTH, DISPARITIES AND EQUITIES 3 UNITS 54 LECTURE HOURS, 108 OUT-OF-CLASS HOURS, 162 TOTAL STUDENT LEARNING HOURS Recommendation for Success: Before enrolling in this course, students are strongly advised to have satisfactorily complete ENGL C1000E or ENGL C1000 or ELIC 100. Examination of personal and social determinants of health through the examination of the role individuals play in their own health and wellbeing, along with the impact of environmental, social, structural, and cultural factors that play a role both in individual and community and public health. Health disparities and inequities in sexually diverse, gender, racial, and minority populations will be explored, and culturally competent ideas to bridge the health equity gap and improve population health will be developed. Not repeatable. Transfer: (CSU, UC). Field trips are not required. (A-F or P/NP) General Education: Using catalog rights, check catalog for course general education approvals. courses.instructor: Steve A. Aristotelous, David L. Shrock, Jim W. Stevens, Michael Girardi, Paul J. Brogan, Kelly Nasrawi, Amanda K. Matis, Zach Hollis, Heidi A. Santino, Shawn A. Black, Jesse Vazquez, Eric D. Fischer
courses.description: HE 110-HEALTHFUL LIVING 3 UNITS, 54 Lecture Hours, 108 Out-of-Class Hours, Total Student Learning Hours=162 This course will require students to explore, analyze, personalize, and discuss the following issues as they relate to the essential components of health and wellness: nutrition, physical activity/exercise/fitness, weight control, eating disorders and body image, media influences, mental health, stress, violence, substance use/abuse, sexuality and sexual orientation, sexually transmitted infections, reproductive choices/contraception, relationships, disease prevention, environment, health care, aging, and general public health issues. Students will be taught the knowledge and skills necessary to implement lifestyle behaviors that can improve their health and well-being. Field trips are not required. Not repeatable.
